name: Insecticides (India) Ltd
title: Insecticides (India) Ltd - 532851 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR2,140 crores while PAT slipped to INR139 crores on a INR9 crore deferred tax charge; Q4 grew about 19%.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of resilience, with full-year revenue up about 7% to INR2,140 crores, gross profit up about 5% to INR675 crores, and EBITDA up about 3% to INR227 crores. PAT fell slightly from INR142 crores to INR139 crores, which management attributed to a roughly INR9 crore increase in deferred tax. Q4 revenue grew about 19%, with premium products up about 24%, but May was sluggish and the company is waiting for monsoon rains. Management guided to positive top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, with the first quarter as the first visible test, while raw material inflation of nearly 10% or more supports pricing.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR142 crores; deferred tax up ~INR9 crores
supported by B2C and B2B; premium products ~24%
per CFO; management also cited FY growth above 7%

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Contributed 73% of FY26 sales. Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C; management targets 60-70% in four years.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Contributed 22% of FY26 sales. Management says B2B held last year's level in April and expects growth in May and the rest of the year.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Contributed 5% of FY26 sales. Management targets 10% in 2-3 years, with CDMO and technical exports as drivers; CDMO work is at trial stage.

segments.name: Product categories (FY26 vs FY25)
segments.commentary: Patented products INR322 crores (vs ~INR330 crores); combination products INR324 crores (vs INR311 crores); in-licensed INR226 crores (vs INR229 crores); 5 products launched in FY26 INR40 crores; FY25 launches rose from INR23 crores to INR82 crores.

segments.name: Herbicides
segments.commentary: Contributed 39% of last year's sales. Price decline from off-patent competition hit last year; management expects quantities and a good increase this year as prices stabilise.

segments.name: Kaeros (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR110-111 crores; PAT above INR5 crores in its second year after acquisition for under INR6 crores. Management expects revenue to at least double in FY27 and contribute 5-8% of IIL volume.

guidance_outlook: Management expects both top line and bottom line to be positive in FY27, with results visible from Q1; management said the number is flat so far and depends on June monsoon.

Management believes the company is well placed to benefit from raw material inflation of up to about 10% or more, since its inventory of close to INR800 crores was bought before the price rise; management expects a small margin increase, with the size dependent on demand.
Management said EBITDA margins have already crossed double digits and it wishes to improve them further, without giving a number.
Working capital cycle target: management called a reduction from 140-150 days to 120 days achievable, with the timing dependent on the season.
Finance cost target: management internally targets a reduction of at least 25-30% in FY27.
Capex for FY27 is largely maintenance, in the range of INR25-30 crores after current projects are completed.
capex_capacity: Dahej: a new building (L&T) has begun manufacturing; management expects it to break even and be profitable by Diwali.
Technical plants at all sites have reached breakeven.
Sotanala: formulation start targeted around Diwali; whether it is billed depends on a CFO investment decision.
Sotanala technical plant: first of two buildings targeted for March-April 2027 for early kharif start; second building to follow based on market yield.
Management says Sotanala and Dahej provide sufficient capacity headroom for growth. About INR94 crores was invested in new products from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Industry: geopolitical tension has created supply constraints; raw material prices rose by nearly 10% and more for crude-linked products, shifting the market to a supplier-driven environment.
Two price increases were taken in April; the first was well received, but the second needed discounts in May. A June price increase is under consideration.
May was sluggish due to heat, and farmers are waiting for monsoon rains; El Nino and crop-mix changes in dry crops are key risks.
Herbicides are gaining traction as manual labour costs rise, but specialty herbicides from competitors are lowering prices.
Management says it sets no write-offs; unsold stock is taken back from the channel at season end and reformulated or moved between regions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from its approximately INR800 crore inventory as raw material prices rise, given smaller competitors may lack stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed, saying the company plans from Diwali to Holi and bought stock before the price rise; the benefit depends on converting that stock into sales as the kharif season starts in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of volume and value growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volume grew 5% and value 14%; FY26 volume grew 5% and value 2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target for the working capital cycle and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle target is 120 days from 140-150 days, which management called achievable. Management internally targets a 25-30% cut in finance cost; the FY26 consolidated finance cost was INR16.87 crores against INR6.86 crores in FY25, driven by higher inventory, bank limit use and INR94 crores of new-product investment.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kaeros positioned against the Tractor/IIL brand and the partner products?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros will run a parallel distribution network with its own brand and a sales-only team. It is positioned as a follower to IIL, which gets first access to partnership products from Corteva, Nissan and OAT. Kaeros is not positioned as a cheaper brand; it will sell at a 2-3% initial discount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of premium products and can it reach 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C. Management targets 60-70% in four years, so 70% will take three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D success rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said success rates vary: about 9,000-10,000 molecules screened a year, with a dozen trial teams testing 500-600 products to yield roughly 10-15 launches. Reverse engineering has higher success rates. The first Indian patent filing is pending IUPAC name approval.

risks_watch: Working capital remains elevated: inventory was higher and DSO is being worked on to reduce it; cash conversion is a stated priority.
Finance cost rose sharply from INR6.86 crores to INR16.87 crores (consolidated); a reduction of 25-30% is the internal target.
Monsoon and El Nino conditions; May was sluggish, and June price increase is not yet decided.
Second April price increase needed discounts in May, showing channel resistance to pricing.
Specialty herbicide competition from off-patent products is putting pressure on prices.
Sotanala formulation and technical plant timelines (Diwali 2026 and March-April 2027) and billing decisions are uncertain.
Kaeros channel conflict risk, as Kaeros is distributed alongside IIL partner products; management says the policy of no common distributors avoids conflict.
Deferred tax charge of about INR9 crores weighed on FY26 PAT.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy, Kaeros and pricing, but cautious on near-term demand; management repeatedly tied outcomes to monsoon and June. It gave no firm numbers on margin, capex or Sotanala billing, and was evasive on the Kaeros revenue question, which it answered in part.
key_quotes: We registered approximately 19% growth in Q4, supported by both B2C and B2B business.
Our long -term strategy of premiumization and differentiated technologies is going with strong traction.
Kaeros will be one of the contributors, which should contribute 5% to 7% - 8% to IIL's volume.
